name: Nihon no Dentou Iro (日本の伝統色)
description: Nihon no Dentou Iro (日本の伝統色) — colors drawn from nature, seasons, and centuries of Japanese aesthetic refinement

foundation.story: Japan's traditional color vocabulary spans over 1,000 named hues, each tied to a natural phenomenon, season, or material. These colors emerged through centuries of textile dyeing, ceramics, and woodblock printing. The palette embodies wabi-sabi — finding beauty in imperfection, impermanence, and depth.
foundation.philosophy: Wabi-sabi (侘寂) — beauty in imperfection, asymmetry, and natural aging

seedColors.name: Hanada (縹)
seedColors.tradition: Japanese indigo dyeing (ai-zome). One of the oldest dye traditions in Japan, using Persicaria tinctoria leaves.
seedColors.source: The Colors of Japan (Nihon no Iro), Kyoto Traditional Arts Foundation

seedColors.name: Sakura-nezumi (桜鼠)
seedColors.tradition: A muted cherry-blossom grey, popular in Edo-period kimono textiles. Captures the fleeting quality of sakura.
seedColors.source: Nihon no Dentou Iro (日本の伝統色辞典)

seedColors.name: Wasurenagusa-iro (勿忘草色)
seedColors.tradition: Forget-me-not blue. A contemplative tone from Meiji-era poetry and botanical illustration.

seedColors.name: Kitsune-iro (狐色)
seedColors.tradition: Fox color — the warm golden-brown of toasted rice and autumn fields. Used in lacquerware and ceramic glazes.

seedColors.name: Enji (臙脂)
seedColors.tradition: Cochineal-derived crimson, introduced via Chinese trade. Prized in formal court garments and temple textiles.
seedColors.source: Colors in Japanese Art, PIE International

seedColors.name: Rikyuu-nezumi (利休鼠)
seedColors.tradition: Named after tea master Sen no Rikyuu. A green-tinted grey embodying tea ceremony restraint.

seedColors.name: Shironeri (白練)
seedColors.tradition: Refined white — the color of raw silk after degumming. Not pure white, but warm and alive.
